propositions: The close gate's undeclared-paths refusal message advertises 'declare paths and retry' as a remedy, but this bare retry fails because declaring paths changes file_impact hash and triggers stale-material refusal
Widening file_impact retroactively broadens the attestation's scope beyond what the reviewer examined, since attestation scope is built from file_impact union cited files
file_impact is a direct input to plan review at four sites (pass1.py, det_lint.py, det_invariants.py, det_gate_rules.py), so new paths can introduce new review findings
The materiality test hashes the entire file_impact list wholesale, making additive changes and destructive edits equally different with no downstream signal to distinguish them
The undeclared-paths message must be clarified to state that declaring new paths is a material plan change requiring rebar review-plan re-attestation before close can succeed
